title: thermite-syntax addressing: oracle string binary_search.loop#1.inv#2 vs verbatim corpus order. spec-routes.toml conformance_ops and the issue-#3 brief say binary_search.loop#1.inv#2 resolves to forall_from(haystack, hi, |x| x > needle), but under 1-based source-order numbering of conformance/binary_search.th the SECOND inv is forall_below(...) and forall_from(...) is inv#3. design 4.3's own example uses loop#1.inv#2 without saying which invariant. Need the conformance/address/ fixture pinned to one reading before the parser builder (#3) runs. .design/syntax/semantic-addressing.md AC-1 currently commits to scheme-authoritative (inv#2=forall_below, inv#3=forall_from); amend the doc if the oracle string is authoritative instead.

comments.content: Filed by acto-doc-author while authoring .design/syntax/semantic-addressing.md. Documented in that doc's OQ-1 + AC-1 NOTE. Releasing lock — this is an orchestrator/critic decision before the #3 builder runs, not doc-author work.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: RESOLVED (orchestrator): adopt the scheme-authoritative reading — 1-based source order counting ALL invariants. For binary_search.loop#1: inv#1 = 'lo <= hi && hi <= haystack.len()', inv#2 = 'forall_below(haystack, lo, |x| x < needle)', inv#3 = 'forall_from(haystack, hi, |x| x > needle)'. semantic-addressing.md AC-1/AC-2 are correct as written. The thermite-design.md §4.3 'forge edit ... inv#2 --replace forall_from(...)' example is an ERRATUM (it labels inv#2 but quotes inv#3's content); §4.3's own prose 'the second invariant' agrees with source-order. The conformance/address/ fixtures will pin this reading. Thesis erratum flagged to the user (not silently patched). OQ-2 (spec-fn dec: no inner address in v0.1) and OQ-3 (nested loops: flat within-function numbering) confirmed as the doc has them.
